definition: Natural language processing is computer activity in which computers are entailed to analyze, understand, alter, or generate natural language.
details: This includes the automation of any or all linguistic forms, activities, or methods of communication, such as conversation, correspondence, reading, written composition, dictation, publishing, translation, lip reading, and so on. Natural-language processing is also the name of the branch of computer science, artificial intelligence, and linguistics concerned with enabling computers to engage in communication using natural language(s) in all forms, including but not limited to speech, print, writing, and signing. The following outline is provided as an overview of and topical guide to natural-language processing:

explainer.lead: Natural language processing is the computer activity of analyzing, understanding, altering, or generating natural language. It spans conversation, reading, writing, translation, and speech in all their forms.

tiers.eli5: It's everything that lets a computer read, write, or talk with human language, from translating a sentence to answering a question.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply NLP across speech, print, and written text for tasks like translation and summarization. The pitfall is ambiguity and context: language meaning shifts with domain, so models need representative data.
tiers.paperLevel: NLP is computer activity in which computers analyze, understand, alter, or generate natural language, covering linguistic forms such as conversation, correspondence, reading, composition, dictation, publishing, translation, and lip reading.

explainer.example: A translation system takes a sentence in one language and produces an equivalent sentence in another.
